docs.title: Shield LDAP User Guide
docs.text:
Shield LDAP adds LDAPv3 and Active Directory sign-in to applications using CodeIgniter Shield. The authenticator verifies directory credentials over LDAPS or StartTLS and completes sign-in through Shield's session and login actions.

Run composer show maniaba/shield-ldap in your application to find its installed version. Use the version selector in the header to find the guide for that release. Select Development if you installed dev-main.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Install the package in an application with Shield configured.
  2. Configure the directory using the Active Directory or OpenLDAP example.
  3. Enable LDAP web login in your application's routes and sign-in form.

docs.title: Guides and References
docs.text:
• Login eligibility covers login attributes, filters, and group-based sign-in restrictions.
  • User management covers provisioning, account linking, hybrid login, and existing sessions.
  • Troubleshooting covers TLS, directory binds, and rejected logins.
  • Configuration reference lists settings, defaults, and limits.
  • Directory diagnostics covers programmatic connection and search checks.
  • Testing explains how to run the package tests and the OpenLDAP integration suite.

For groups, permissions, and other authentication methods, see the Shield User Guide.

docs.title: LDAP and Active Directory Authentication
docs.text:
The Shield LDAP User Guide contains the setup instructions and reference for the maniaba/shield-ldap package.

  • Installation covers requirements and Composer.
  • Configuration covers Active Directory, OpenLDAP, and TLS.
  • Using LDAP Authentication connects your application's web login to LDAP.
  • Login Eligibility covers sign-in and group filters.
  • User Management covers provisioning, account linking, and hybrid login.
  • Directory Diagnostics covers connection and search checks.
  • Troubleshooting covers common configuration and login problems.
  • Testing covers the OpenLDAP integration suite.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Create app/Config/AuthLDAP.php by extending the package's AuthLDAP class. Use the $connections property for directory settings and standard CodeIgniter environment overrides for deployment-specific values. LDAP sign-in is disabled by default. Enable it after configuring your directory and web login.

docs.title: Prepare the Directory and PHP Runtime
docs.text:
1. Create a read-only service account that can search within the configured user base and read login attributes, immutable IDs, and attributes used by filters or profile mappings.

  2. Configure trust for the directory's CA in the OpenLDAP client settings used by PHP. You can use the following settings in the client configuration file, commonly /etc/ldap/ldap.conf.

    TLS_CACERT /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ldap-ca.pem
TLS_REQCERT demand
TLS_REQSAN demand

  3. Confirm that the certificates presented by all endpoints are valid for the configured hostnames and chain to a trusted CA. Mount the CA bundle in the web runtime and restart PHP workers after updating their trust settings. A service manager can supply the CA path through the LDAPTLS_CACERT process environment variable. See the OpenLDAP TLS reference.

Use ldaps for listeners that negotiate TLS as soon as they accept a connection (normally port 636). Use starttls for listeners that accept the LDAP StartTLS operation before bind (normally port 389). The native transport requires TLS validation and rejects referrals. Each process uses the same OpenLDAP client trust policy for its configured directories.

docs.title: Active Directory
docs.text:
The following configuration searches two domain controllers in order. Users can sign in with sAMAccountName or userPrincipalName. The login filter excludes disabled accounts and objectGUID provides the immutable identity.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Config;

use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Config\AuthLDAP as ShieldAuthLDAP;

class AuthLDAP extends ShieldAuthLDAP
{
    public string $defaultConnection = 'corporate';

    public array $connections = [
        'corporate' => [
            'hosts'               => ['dc01.example.com', 'dc02.example.com'],
            'baseDn'              => 'DC=example,DC=com',
            'bindDn'              => 'CN=shield-reader,OU=Service Accounts,DC=example,DC=com',
            'bindPassword'        => '',
            'encryption'          => 'ldaps',
            'port'                => 636,
            'userBaseDn'          => 'OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com',
            'loginFilter'         => '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user)(!(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=2)))',
            'loginAttributes'     => ['sAMAccountName', 'userPrincipalName'],
            'externalIdAttribute' => 'objectGUID',
            'profileAttributes'   => ['username' => 'sAMAccountName'],
            'provisionUsers'      => true,
        ],
    ];
}

Supply the password and enable LDAP through .env.

authldap.enabled = true
authldap.connections.corporate.bindPassword = 'replace-with-service-account-password'

docs.title: OpenLDAP
docs.text:
For an OpenLDAP server with StartTLS, use the following app/Config/AuthLDAP.php. This example looks up users by uid and links their Shield accounts by entryUUID. Allow the service account to read that operational attribute.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Config;

use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Config\AuthLDAP as ShieldAuthLDAP;

class AuthLDAP extends ShieldAuthLDAP
{
    public string $defaultConnection = 'openldap';

    public array $connections = [
        'openldap' => [
            'hosts'               => ['ldap.example.org'],
            'baseDn'              => 'dc=example,dc=org',
            'bindDn'              => 'cn=shield-reader,ou=services,dc=example,dc=org',
            'bindPassword'        => '',
            'encryption'          => 'starttls',
            'port'                => 389,
            'userBaseDn'          => 'ou=people,dc=example,dc=org',
            'loginFilter'         => '(objectClass=inetOrgPerson)',
            'loginAttributes'     => ['uid'],
            'externalIdAttribute' => 'entryUUID',
            'profileAttributes'   => ['username' => 'uid'],
            'provisionUsers'      => true,
        ],
    ];
}

Supply the password under the connection ID openldap.

authldap.enabled = true
authldap.connections.openldap.bindPassword = 'replace-with-service-account-password'

For another LDAPv3 server, choose the login attributes, filters, and immutable identifier according to its schema. The identifier must be unique, readable, and stable across account renames and moves. See Login Eligibility and the configuration reference.

docs.title: Environment Overrides
docs.text:
Keep .env outside version control. When a deployment environment requires underscores in variable names, use keys such as authldap_connections_corporate_bindPassword. The normal CodeIgniter config initialization applies these overrides. Declare the connection ID and each option before setting its environment override. The same rule applies to list entries, such as authldap.connections.corporate.hosts.0.

Warning

Direct reads of $connections, configuration exports, and CodeIgniter's configuration cache can expose the bind password. Use an application-owned connection provider if the password must stay outside the configuration cache.

docs.title: Multiple Directories
docs.text:
List replicas of one directory in a single connection's hosts, in preference order. Give independent directories separate connection IDs. If users enter UPNs from different directories, map each lower-case suffix to a connection ID.

public array $loginDomains = [
    'example.com'          => 'corporate',
    'research.example.org' => 'research',
];

Declare corporate and research under $connections before using this example. The default connection handles unqualified identifiers and unmapped suffixes. The selected connection looks up the entire submitted identifier, including any suffix. Keep connection IDs stable because they identify the scope of the link between a directory account and a Shield user.

Continue to Using LDAP Authentication to register the authenticator and connect it to your application's login form.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: These instructions assume you have a CodeIgniter 4 application, a configured .env file, and a database that the Spark CLI can access.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Supported versions PHP ^8.2 (PHP 8.2 or later in the 8.x series) CodeIgniter 4 >=4.3.5 <4.5.0 or ^4.5.1 CodeIgniter Shield ^1.4.1 (Shield 1.4.1 or later in the 1.x series) Composer Required to install the package and its dependencies PHP LDAP extension A build linked against OpenLDAP is required for the native directory service

Check the LDAP extension with php --ri ldap. If your application runs through PHP-FPM or another web runtime, check that runtime's extension configuration as well. An application that supplies its own directory transport can use the dependencies required by that transport.

docs.title: Set Up Shield
docs.text: If Shield is new to your application, follow the Shield installation guide to install it, publish its configuration, and set up its database tables. Shield LDAP uses the existing Shield user, identity, and login tables.

docs.title: Stable Release
docs.text:
Install a stable release from Packagist once one is available. Run Composer from your application's root directory.

composer require maniaba/shield-ldap

To keep the application on the Shield 1.4 release series, use an explicit Shield constraint when installing the package.

composer require 'codeigniter4/shield:~1.4.1' maniaba/shield-ldap

docs.title: Development Branch
docs.text:
To install the development branch from Packagist, require its version explicitly.

composer require maniaba/shield-ldap:dev-main

Select Development in the guide's version selector when using this branch.

Composer resolves the package against the version constraints in your application. If a Shield constraint blocks installation, run composer why codeigniter4/shield to see which packages impose it.

Continue to Configuration to set up directory access.

docs.title: Login Eligibility
docs.text: Configure the filters for each directory in app/Config/AuthLDAP.php. See Configuration for complete Active Directory and OpenLDAP examples.

docs.title: Login and Eligibility Filters
docs.text:
• loginFilter narrows the initial search for a directory entry. The authenticator combines this filter with equality checks for the submitted identifier across the configured loginAttributes. It requires exactly one matching entry. Case matching follows the directory's equality rule.
  • eligibilityFilter adds an access check after the user bind succeeds. The native transport applies both filters to the matched entry and verifies its immutable identity again before resolving the Shield user.

Apply rules that define the directory's population to loginFilter. Add application-specific access rules, such as required group membership, to eligibilityFilter. A directory match must still pass Shield's local account checks and any configured login action.

docs.title: Active Directory
docs.text:
Use this eligibilityFilter to exclude disabled accounts and require transitive membership in the Shield Users security group. Replace the group DN with the one used in your directory.

(&(!(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=2))(memberOf:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:=CN=Shield Users,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com))

The bitwise matching rule 1.2.840.113556.1.4.803 tests the disabled bit in userAccountControl. The transitive matching rule 1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941 follows directory links. Verify that the directory links connect eligible users to the configured group. AD stores primary group membership separately, so test it explicitly if an access rule depends on it. Active Directory search filter syntax

docs.title: OpenLDAP
docs.text:
For OpenLDAP with a memberOf overlay, the following eligibilityFilter requires direct membership in shield-users. Nested membership depends on the installed directory schema and overlays.

(memberOf=cn=shield-users,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org)

docs.title: Building Filters in Application Code
docs.text:
Use trusted configuration for LDAP filter expressions. In application code, use LDAPFilter::equal() for runtime assertion values. It escapes wildcards and other special bytes according to RFC 4515. Use all(), any(), and not() to combine complete filters. Keep attribute names and raw filter expressions under application control.

use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\LDAP\LDAPFilter;

$identifier = 'alice@example.com';

$filter = LDAPFilter::all(
    '(objectClass=inetOrgPerson)',
    LDAPFilter::any(
        LDAPFilter::equal('uid', $identifier),
        LDAPFilter::equal('mail', $identifier),
    ),
);

If you construct a DN from a runtime naming value, encode the naming component with LDAPFilter::escapeDnComponent(). Pass the completed DN to equal() to apply filter assertion escaping as well. RFC 4514

use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\LDAP\LDAPFilter;

$groupName = 'Family, Given';
$groupDn   = 'CN=' . LDAPFilter::escapeDnComponent($groupName)
    . ',OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com';

$filter = LDAPFilter::equal('memberOf', $groupDn);

LDAPFilter::validate() checks filter syntax. To verify server-side schema, matching rules, and access, run a bounded directory search. Administrative Diagnostics

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: The browser receives Shield's generic authentication error. For failed directory sign-ins that reach the transport or resolver, Shield LDAP emits the debug message Shield LDAP login rejected ({reason}). with a short reason code. Use an appropriately restricted log when troubleshooting. The diagnostics API also exposes reason codes without returning native LDAP diagnostic messages to the browser.

docs.title: LDAP Client and TLS
docs.text:
Check the PHP process serving the application for the ldap extension and its OpenLDAP TLS settings. The CLI and web server can load different PHP configurations.

php --ri ldap
  • extension_unavailable or unsupported_ldap_client means the runtime needs the PHP LDAP extension and a supported OpenLDAP client.
  • For tls_verification_required, tls_failed, or certificate_verification_failed, check the CA chain, hostname in the certificate's subject alternative name, and client trust settings.
  • For directory_unavailable or connection_timeout, check hostname resolution, network access, and the endpoint port. Some runtime TLS errors also appear as directory_unavailable. Verify trust settings before assuming a network failure.

Use the same endpoint, service DN, and client trust settings as the web runtime. This command prompts for the service password.

ldapsearch -H ldaps://dc01.example.com:636 -x \
  -D 'CN=shield-reader,OU=Service Accounts,DC=example,DC=com' -W \
  -b 'DC=example,DC=com' -s base '(objectClass=*)' dn

For StartTLS, use an ldap:// URI and -ZZ to require the TLS upgrade.

ldapsearch -H ldap://ldap.example.org:389 -ZZ -x \
  -D 'cn=shield-reader,ou=services,dc=example,dc=org' -W \
  -b 'dc=example,dc=org' -s base '(objectClass=*)' dn

docs.title: Service Bind and Directory Search
docs.text:
For service_bind_failed, verify the service DN, deployed credential, and directory policy. For invalid_bind_secret, confirm that the connection defines a nonempty bind password and that the environment overrides the correct configuration key. Configuration

For search_timeout or incomplete_search, check the user search base, directory size limits, and whether the search spans naming contexts. Use a more selective base or filter. The native transport rejects referrals and incomplete login result sets.

For user_not_found, ambiguous_user, or ineligible_user, preview the login and eligibility filters with the same service account. Check the search base, readable login attributes, and rules that determine account eligibility. An identifier must resolve to exactly one entry. Login Eligibility

docs.title: Shield User and Login Action
docs.text:
• invalid_external_identity or invalid_identity indicates a missing, multi-valued, or malformed identifier on the matched entry. Confirm that the configured attribute is readable and single-valued. For Active Directory, the expected objectGUID is a 16-byte value.
  • user_not_provisioned means the entry has no Shield identity link and provisioning is off. Follow the account linking procedure.
  • For identity_conflict, invalid_profile, or synchronization_conflict, check for a username collision, multi-valued attributes, and profile fields permitted by the user provider. The user model and identity model must share the same Shield database connection.
  • If directory credentials pass, also check the local Shield user for a ban or pending activation. If sign-in reaches a login action, verify that its routes and the required user contact identity are configured. Shield web login

docs.title: Managing LDAP Users
docs.text: Shield LDAP links a Shield user to a directory account by the connection ID and an immutable directory identifier. Use objectGUID for Active Directory or entryUUID for OpenLDAP. Keep connection IDs stable. Place replicas of one directory under the same connection ID and configure independent directories under separate IDs. A rename or DN change preserves the existing link when the entry still meets the directory search and eligibility rules.

docs.title: Provisioning Users at Login
docs.text:
Set 'provisionUsers' => true in a connection's configuration to create a Shield user after a successful password bind and eligibility check. Map the local username to a single-valued directory attribute that produces unique, valid Shield usernames of at most 30 characters.

Configure profileAttributes as a map from local fields to LDAP attributes. For example, after adding directory_email and first_name as writable fields in your application's user provider, set the following connection option. Shield user provider

'profileAttributes' => [
    'username'        => 'sAMAccountName',
    'directory_email' => 'mail',
    'first_name'      => 'givenName',
],

Mapped attributes must have at most one value. If a mapped attribute has no value, the mapping skips that field. Set 'updateProfile' => false to apply the mapping only when provisioning. The mapper leaves unmapped fields and Shield's password and email identities under application control. Store directory contact information in a dedicated profile field such as directory_email.

Note

Shield may require a local activation step. When registration activation is configured, an application operator must activate a newly provisioned user through the application's trusted workflow. For login actions, use a contact identity verified by your application or an action that supports directory-only users. Shield authentication actions

docs.title: Linking an Existing Shield User
docs.text:
During migration, start with provisioning disabled. In a trusted operator workflow, verify the directory account and select the Shield user who owns it. Then create the link using the verified external identifier and selected Shield user ID.

use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\LDAP\LDAPUserResolver;

$resolver = new LDAPUserResolver(auth()->getProvider());
$resolver->link('corporate', '00112233-4455-6677-8899-aabbccddeeff', 42);

This example links a canonical AD GUID to Shield user ID 42. If you read the binary objectGUID from LDAP, convert it with LDAPUserResolver::normalizeObjectGuid() first. For OpenLDAP, use the entryUUID returned by the directory.

An existing link to another local user prevents the operation. A username collision also blocks provisioning or profile updates until the conflict is resolved. The resolver owns its write transaction, so call it outside any active transaction on the Shield database connection.

docs.title: Local, LDAP, and Hybrid Login
docs.text:
• Local-only uses Shield's ordinary Session authenticator and login routes.
  • LDAP-only uses the LDAP web login routes and leaves $localAccounts empty.
  • Hybrid uses those LDAP routes and reserves explicit local login identifiers in app/Config/AuthLDAP.php. Each identifier maps to the expected Shield user ID.
public array $localAccounts = ['local-operator' => 10];

A reserved identifier is matched case-insensitively and checked against the named local Shield account. Configure a Shield login MFA action for each reserved operator and confirm they can complete it during an LDAP outage. The authenticator requires a pending login action for a reserved account before establishing a session. Every other identifier is checked by the selected LDAP directory. Rejected directory credentials and outages both deny a new LDAP login.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: Directory group filters control who may sign in. Manage groups and permissions with Shield authorization, including assignment of any groups your application requires for new users.

docs.title: Account Disabling and Password Recovery
docs.text:
Directory eligibility is checked during password login. When disabling an account in the directory, use your application's established procedures to revoke its existing Shield sessions and API tokens when immediate access removal is required.

The authenticator uses the submitted directory password for verification. Shield stores the directory identity link and the mapped profile fields. A directory-only user recovers their password through the directory. Scope Shield's force-reset filter to users with a Shield email/password identity if your Shield version requires that identity for a reset check. Shield force-reset compatibility

For an LDAP-only application, review existing remember-me cookies and alternative login paths during migration. The LDAP authenticator issues no remember-me token. Keep Shield's allowRemembering disabled and revoke pre-migration tokens according to your application's policies.

docs.title: Using the LDAP Authenticator
docs.text: Use this guide to add an LDAP sign-in form to an application that has completed Shield setup and configured a directory connection. For existing accounts, follow the user management guide to link a directory identity before testing sign-in.

docs.title: Register the Authenticator
docs.text:
In app/Config/Auth.php, add ldap to the existing $authenticators array. Keep any aliases already in use. Keep $defaultAuthenticator set to 'session' so Shield's login view, logout, and session filters use the session established by LDAP.

public array $authenticators = [
    'tokens'  => \CodeIgniter\Shield\Authentication\Authenticators\AccessTokens::class,
    'session' => \CodeIgniter\Shield\Authentication\Authenticators\Session::class,
    'hmac'    => \CodeIgniter\Shield\Authentication\Authenticators\HmacSha256::class,
    'ldap'    => \Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\Authenticators\LDAP::class,
];

In the same file, set the login entry in the existing $views array to '\App\Views\auth\ldap_login' and set the allowRemembering entry in $sessionConfig to false. The following settings hide the registration and magic-link links, which the example routes omit.

public bool $allowRegistration = false;
public bool $allowMagicLinkLogins = false;

docs.title: Create the Login View
docs.text:
Copy vendor/codeigniter4/shield/src/Views/login.php to app/Views/auth/ldap_login.php. Replace the email input and its label with a text input named username. This accepts a short account name such as alice or a user principal name such as alice@example.com, depending on your directory configuration. Keep Shield's password input and CSRF field.

<label for="ldapUsername"><?= lang('Auth.username') ?></label>
<input id="ldapUsername" type="text" name="username" autocomplete="username" required>

docs.title: Create the Login Action
docs.text:
Add the following method to an application controller. This example uses app/Controllers/Login.php. It submits credentials to LDAP and sends users with a pending Shield login action to the action's form before allowing access to the application.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Controllers;

use CodeIgniter\HTTP\RedirectResponse;
use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\Authenticators\LDAP;

final class Login extends BaseController
{
    public function loginAction(): RedirectResponse
    {
        /** @var LDAP $ldap */
        $ldap   = auth('ldap')->getAuthenticator();
        $result = $ldap->attempt($this->request->getPost(['username', 'password']));

        if (! $result->isOK()) {
            return redirect()->route('login')->with('error', $result->reason());
        }

        return $ldap->hasAction()
            ? redirect()->route('auth-action-show')->withCookies()
            : redirect()->to(config('Auth')->loginRedirect())->withCookies();
    }
}

Warning

Keep the failure redirect limited to the error message. CodeIgniter's withInput() can copy the submitted password into session flash data. Set zend.exception_ignore_args=On in production to keep credentials out of application exception traces.

docs.title: Register the Routes
docs.text:
In app/Config/Routes.php, replace the service('auth')->routes($routes) call added by Shield setup with the following. If your application already passes route options, merge the exclusions into that call.

service('auth')->routes($routes, ['except' => ['login', 'register', 'magic-link']]);

$routes->get('login', '\CodeIgniter\Shield\Controllers\LoginController::loginView', ['as' => 'login']);
$routes->post('login', '\App\Controllers\Login::loginAction', ['filter' => 'auth-rates']);

In app/Config/Security.php, set $csrfProtection to 'session'. In app/Config/Filters.php, enable csrf in the global before filters. Keep the login and authentication action POST routes covered by that filter. If you apply Shield's session filter globally, exclude login and auth/a/* so users can reach the form and complete login actions.

Review the route table with php spark routes. On versions such as Shield 1.4.1, the default auth/a/* routes leave rate limiting to the application. If those routes have no auth-rates filter, add the following entry to the existing $filters array in app/Config/Filters.php. Shield registers the filter alias.

public array $filters = [
    'auth-rates' => ['before' => ['auth/a/show', 'auth/a/handle', 'auth/a/verify']],
];

See Shield's controller filters for session protection and rate limiting.

docs.title: Configure Login Actions
docs.text:
Shield runs the login action configured in the login entry of Config\Auth::$actions when it applies to the user. To enable Shield's built-in email verification, set that entry to \CodeIgniter\Shield\Authentication\Actions\Email2FA::class.

Email2FA uses the address in the user's local Shield email identity. Set up an independently verified address for each user and configure mail delivery in app/Config/Email.php before enabling the action. For directory users provisioned without an email identity, choose an action that supports those accounts. Configure an applicable MFA action for each reserved local account if you use hybrid sign-in.

See Shield's authentication actions.

docs.title: Test Sign-in
docs.text:
1. Make sure authldap.enabled = true. Enable provisioning for the test connection or link the test directory account to the correct Shield user.
  2. Visit /login in a fresh browser session. Sign in with a known test account and complete any login action, then confirm that a route protected by the session filter is accessible.
  3. Sign out and try an incorrect password. Check that the login form shows a generic error and that the protected route still requires sign-in.

See Troubleshooting if sign-in fails.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Define LDAP settings in app/Config/AuthLDAP.php. Each entry in $connections is an array of options for one directory. The array key becomes the connection ID. See the configuration guide for complete Active Directory and OpenLDAP examples.

docs.title: AuthLDAP
docs.text:
Property Default Description $enabled false Enables password sign-in through the LDAP authenticator. $defaultConnection '' Selects a connection for login identifiers without a mapped UPN suffix. $connections [] Directory settings keyed by connection ID. Use 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. Start with a letter or digit. $loginDomains [] Maps lowercase UPN suffixes to connection IDs. The full submitted identifier is still used for the directory search. $localAccounts [] Maps reserved login identifiers to Shield user IDs for hybrid login. Identifiers are matched case-insensitively.

The default config builds and validates a connection when getConnection() is called. Use connectionIds() to list configured IDs.

docs.title: Connection Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description hosts Required Ordered list of 1 to 10 hostnames or IP addresses. Specify IPv6 addresses without brackets. baseDn Required Base DN of the directory naming context. bindDn Required DN of the read-only lookup account. bindPassword Required Nonempty service-account password. Use an environment override or an application-owned provider. encryption 'ldaps' Use 'ldaps' or 'starttls'. port null Integer from 1 to 65535. With null, LDAPS uses 636 and StartTLS uses 389. connectTimeout 5 Network connection timeout in seconds, from 1 to 60. searchTimeout 5 LDAP operation and search time limit in seconds, from 1 to 60. userBaseDn null Base DN for user lookups. With null, lookups use baseDn. loginFilter '(objectClass=person)' Trusted LDAP filter for the initial user lookup. loginAttributes ['uid'] List of 1 to 10 LDAP attributes accepted as a login identifier. The directory evaluates equality using its schema rules. externalIdAttribute 'entryUUID' Immutable, single-valued LDAP attribute used to link the Shield user. Use objectGUID for Active Directory. profileAttributes [] Map of writable Shield user fields to single-valued directory attributes. Map username when provisioning users. provisionUsers false Creates a Shield user on successful LDAP sign-in when there is no existing link. eligibilityFilter '(objectClass=*)' Additional trusted filter evaluated on the matched entry after password verification. updateProfile true Updates mapped attributes on existing linked users during successful directory checks. When false, mappings still apply on provisioning.

Keep endpoints in a connection within one logical directory and apply equivalent access policies on every endpoint. The native transport tries endpoints in the listed order during connection setup. An unavailable endpoint or a timeout can advance to the next endpoint. Certificate verification failures stop the operation. After the initial service bind, the user lookup, password verification, and eligibility check stay on that endpoint. See Troubleshooting for common connection errors.

docs.title: Login and Eligibility Filters
docs.text:
The initial lookup combines loginFilter with an OR of escaped equality tests for every entry in loginAttributes. The native transport requires exactly one entry, verifies the password, and checks the original lookup filter and eligibilityFilter against the same immutable directory identity.

See Login Eligibility for Active Directory and OpenLDAP examples, including disabled accounts and group membership.

docs.title: Building Filters
docs.text: LDAPFilter::validate() checks syntax, a maximum of 16,384 bytes, and up to 32 nested expressions. Use directory diagnostics to check server-side schema, matching rules, and attribute access. See Building Filters in Application Code for examples using runtime values and DN components.

docs.title: Directory Diagnostics
docs.text:
Use the ldapDirectory service from an administrative command or another trusted application workflow. It exposes connectivity, service-account bind, bounded search, and directory credential checks.

Important

Apply authorization, CSRF protection, and rate limiting to any web interface that calls these methods. Limit operators to approved connection IDs, search bases, and attributes. Keep results, submitted passwords, and native directory error details out of application logs.

docs.title: Check a Connection
docs.text:
use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Config\AuthLDAP;
use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Exceptions\LDAPException;

/** @var AuthLDAP $config */
$config = config('AuthLDAP');

$connectionIds = $config->connectionIds();
$directory     = service('ldapDirectory');

try {
    $connection = $config->getConnection('corporate');
    $directory->testConnection($connection);
    $directory->testBind($connection);
} catch (LDAPException $exception) {
    log_message('warning', 'LDAP connection check failed ({reason}).', ['reason' => $exception->reason]);
}

testConnection() checks connectivity with TLS verification. For LDAPS, the native transport uses an anonymous Root DSE query to trigger the handshake. testBind() establishes a connection and verifies the service-account credentials. Both return after success and throw LDAPException on failure. The exception's reason property contains a diagnostic code suitable for operator logs. See Troubleshooting for how to interpret connection and sign-in failures.

docs.title: Preview Directory Entries
docs.text:
The following example requests display names from a configured Active Directory user search. Use a trusted group search base and group filter with the same method to inspect group entries.

use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\LDAP\LDAPFilter;

$entries = $directory->preview(
    $connection,
    $connection->userBaseDn ?? $connection->baseDn,
    LDAPFilter::all($connection->loginFilter, $connection->eligibilityFilter),
    ['sAMAccountName', 'displayName'],
    20,
);

The native transport accepts a limit from 1 to 100 and up to 64 attribute names. Pass an empty attribute list for DNs alone. Each result has a dn and an attributes map with lowercase attribute names and lists of values. Values such as objectGUID may be binary.

A full page of results can indicate that the limit was reached. Use the method only to sample entries. Search referrals and unexpected partial results raise an LDAPException.

docs.title: Check a User's Directory Credentials
docs.text:
Use the directory service to check a password and eligibility without creating a Shield session or updating a Shield account. The application supplies the trusted connection and a login identifier and password from the operator's request.

use Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\LDAP\LDAPFilter;

$matches = [];

foreach ($connection->loginAttributes as $attribute) {
    $matches[] = LDAPFilter::equal($attribute, $identifier);
}

$entry = $directory->authenticate(
    $connection,
    $connection->userBaseDn ?? $connection->baseDn,
    LDAPFilter::all($connection->loginFilter, LDAPFilter::any(...$matches)),
    [],
    $password,
    $connection->eligibilityFilter,
);

The native implementation returns the verified entry and includes the configured immutable ID attribute in the result. It throws LDAPException if it cannot verify a single eligible user. Discard the password after the operation and show the operator only the information needed for diagnosis.

Note

auth('ldap')->check() resolves a Shield user and may provision or update that user. For application sign-in, use auth('ldap')->attempt() and complete the configured Shield login actions. See the LDAP login quick start.

docs.title: Custom Connection Providers
docs.text:
Extend the package's AuthLDAP config in app/Config/AuthLDAP.php and override getConnection(string $id): LDAPConnection and connectionIds(): array to load settings from your application. In getConnection(), resolve the requested ID and read the service password from the application's secret store. Pass the password as a string to LDAPConnection with the same ID that was requested. Use LDAPException('invalid_configuration') for unrecognized IDs.

This allows the application to keep the password outside CodeIgniter's config cache. Return only connection IDs or approved operational metadata to an administrator interface.

docs.title: Replacing the Transport
docs.text:
CodeIgniter discovers the package's ldapDirectory service automatically. To provide a different directory transport, implement Maniaba\ShieldLDAP\Authentication\LDAP\LDAPDirectoryInterface and declare a ldapDirectory() service in app/Config/Services.php. Follow the CodeIgniter Services guide.

An implementation used for sign-in must verify the submitted password over a trusted encrypted connection, require one matching user, and recheck the same immutable identity against the eligibility filter. Return the entry DN and the requested attribute values using lowercase keys and lists of strings. Throw LDAPException with a reason code instead of passing native exceptions or credentials to the application.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Run the following commands from a Shield LDAP checkout with Composer and the PHP extensions required by CodeIgniter. Enable SQLite3 for the default test database.

composer install
composer test

composer test runs the main PHPUnit suite. It covers configuration, filters, authentication, account provisioning, and Shield's web session lifecycle using directory doubles. It runs without a live LDAP server. SQLite3 is sufficient for local development. The PHPUnit workflow runs the suite across PHP versions and database drivers. The compatibility workflow checks selected Shield releases.

docs.title: Code Checks
docs.text:
Use the same CodeIgniter coding standard and analysis tools used by Shield.

composer cs
composer analyze
composer inspect

composer cs checks formatting with PHP-CS-Fixer. Use composer cs-fix to apply formatting. composer analyze runs PHPStan, Psalm, and Rector in check mode. composer inspect runs StructArmed. To run these checks with the main test suite, use composer ci.

docs.title: OpenLDAP Integration Tests
docs.text:
Install Docker and OpenSSL and enable PHP's LDAP extension linked against OpenLDAP in the CLI runtime. Run the same integration suite as the OpenLDAP workflow.

composer test:ldap

The runner builds the fixture under tests/_support/LDAP/ and starts it with temporary certificates on loopback ports. It waits for service-account binds over LDAPS and StartTLS, runs the ldap-integration PHPUnit suite, and stops the container when the run finishes. A failed smoke check, empty suite, or skipped test fails the run.

Add live OpenLDAP tests under tests/Authentication/LDAP/Integration/. PHPUnit discovers the tests there as part of the integration suite.

For Active Directory changes, also exercise the setup against a disposable AD DS or Samba AD test domain. Confirm GUID handling after an account rename, disabled-account filters, transitive membership, and the configured TLS certificate policy in the directory you deploy against. See the configuration reference.
